thread.title: Apple iPhone XS Preorders Off To Slow Start, Below iPhone X

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple iPhone XS Preorders Off To Slow Start, Below iPhone X
text:
Apple ( AAPL ) began taking preorders for its iPhone XS and iPhone XS Max on Friday and early indications point to a quiet start for sales of the company's 12th-generation smartphones. The new handsets will be available for purchase starting Friday.
X Rosenblatt Securities analyst Jun Zhang estimates Apple received about 10 million preorders for iPhone XS series handsets in the first three days. He based his estimate on current wait times of roughly one to two weeks in most regions and estimated weekly production volumes.
"We believe iPhone XS and iPhone XS Max preorders to be weaker compared to the iPhone X preorders, which we had estimated last year to be about 12 million in the first three days, with lead times of 3-5 weeks," Zhang said in a note to clients Monday.
Apple stock fell 2.7% to 217.88 on the stock market today .
U.S. Preorders Similar To Last Year Apple is likely to produce 35 million to 36 million units of the iPhone XS and iPhone XS Max in the calendar third and fourth quarters, Zhang said. That compares with the estimated 36 million units of the iPhone X that Apple produced during the same period last year, he said.
The Cupertino, Calif.-based consumer electronics giant introduced its new smartphones at a media event last Wednesday. It also showed off its fourth-generation smartwatch with enhanced health and fitness features. The Apple Watch Series 4 goes on sale Friday alongside the new iPhones.
Apple introduced its iPhone X on Sept. 12, 2017, exactly one year before the current iPhone XS. But the iPhone X launch was marred by production issues that limited supply of the 11th-generation handset. It went on sale on Nov. 3 after a week of preorders.
Analysts say the iPhone X failed to meet lofty sales expectations at first, but proved to be a consistent seller afterward.
Will Ramp Up Normally: Analyst Nomura Instinet analyst Jeffrey Kvaal said preorders of the new iPhones in the U.S. are on par with last year's models.
"Our work on the first weekend of orders for the XS and Max indicates both U.S. telco promos and iPhone shipment times are similar to 2017," he said in a report Sunday. "Given the rapid international rollout, we believe Apple expects supply for all models to ramp normally (unlike with the X)."
U.S. wireless carriers AT&T ( T ), T-Mobile ( TMUS ) and Verizon ( VZ ) all are offering a $700 credit on a new iPhone, but the deals require the addition of a new line, he said.
